content_summary: Pinned this library for our scraping pipeline and the HTML-to-text call now blows up on every input under a recent Python, so we vendored our own stripper for the time being.
The insertion-ordered set is lovely until you delete something; after that the slices we take for paging quietly stop lining up with what iteration shows.
Spent an afternoon on a test that would not fail: comparing the multi-value dict against a plain dict seems to look at keys and shrug at the values.
Would happily switch our repo scanner over if the recursive file search could be told how deep to go; walking a full monorepo just to read the top level is a hard sell.
Small thing, but our capacity dashboards read 1024K and 1024M all over the place, which makes the round numbers look like formatting bugs to reviewers.
The text table renderer is handy for CLI output, though columns go ragged as soon as one cell is much longer than its neighbours, so we post-process the result.
